meta.title: Who originally recorded "You Got the Love"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not Florence + the Machine. It was first released in 1986 by The Source featuring Candi Staton on Streetwave — and it did not chart.
meta.ogTitle: Who originally recorded 'You Got the Love'?
meta.ogDescription: Florence + the Machine's 2009 hit is a cover. The first release was The Source featuring Candi Staton, Streetwave, 1986.

answer.label: Not a Florence + the Machine original — a 1986 single by The Source featuring Candi Staton on Streetwave
answer.originalArtistDates: Candi Staton, b. 13 March 1940, Hanceville, Alabama · American soul and gospel singer · The Source was a British songwriting trio
answer.sourceLine: A very large audience first heard this song in 2009 and files it as a Florence + the Machine song. It is a cover. The first record was “You Got the Love” by The Source featuring Candi Staton, issued as a 12″ single on Morgan Khan’s Streetwave label in the UK in 1986, and it was written by Anthony B. Stephens, Arnecia Michelle Harris and John Bellamy — the three men and women who were The Source. The 1986 record did not chart; the song only became a hit five years later, when a bootleg mix of Staton’s vocal reached No. 4 in Britain in 1991.

original.heading: Who recorded it first
original.label: Streetwave
original.released: Issued in 1986 as a 12″ vinyl single in the UK on Morgan Khan’s Streetwave label, catalogue number MKHAN 78, credited to The Source featuring Candi Staton. The A-side carried an extended vocal running about six and three-quarter minutes plus a radio edit; the B-side held a club house mix and an a cappella. DJ Simon Harris had found and licensed the track that year while looking for material for his newly formed Music of Life label, and took it to Khan.
original.charted: Did not chart. The Official Charts Company’s history for The Source contains no 1986 entry at all — its first listing for the act is 2 February 1991, when the bootleg remix reached No. 4, followed by a No. 3 peak in 1997.
original.writer: Anthony B. Stephens, Arnecia Michelle Harris and John Bellamy
original.cover: Florence + the Machine’s “You’ve Got the Love” on Island Records, produced by Charlie Hugall. It appeared as a B-side to “Dog Days Are Over” on 1 December 2008, as a UK digital single on 5 January 2009 and as a physical reissue on 16 November 2009. It peaked at No. 5 on the UK Singles Chart, spent 30 weeks there, and is certified 5× Platinum in the UK.

trail: Wikipedia’s article on the single ↗ states that the song was written by Anthony B. Stephens, Arnecia Michelle Harris and John Bellamy, that Simon Harris licensed it in 1986, and that it was released on Morgan Khan’s Streetwave label — and that Staton’s vocal had been recorded earlier for a direct-to-video documentary she had forgotten making.
The physical object is catalogued: MusicBrainz lists the 1986 UK Streetwave 12″ ↗, catalogue MKHAN 78, credited to The Source feat. Candi Staton, with four mixes across the two sides.
The chart record confirms the original was a commercial non-starter: the Official Charts Company’s history for The Source ↗ begins on 2 February 1991 at No. 4, with no 1986 entry.

That the act and the writers are the same people is confirmed by Wikipedia’s entry on The Source ↗, which describes the name as an alias for the Stephens–Harris–Bellamy songwriting team before John Truelove adopted it in 1991.

authors.name: The Source featuring Candi Staton
authors.heading: The Source featuring Candi Staton
authors.metaLine: British production/songwriting trio with American singer Candi Staton (b. 13 March 1940) · Streetwave, 1986
authors.bio: “The Source” began as an alias for the British songwriting team of Anthony B. Stephens, Arnecia Michelle Harris and John Bellamy, per Wikipedia’s entry on the group ↗. The voice on the record is Candi Staton, the Alabama-born soul and gospel singer already known in America for her 1970 reading of “Stand by Your Man” and her 1976 disco hit “Young Hearts Run Free.” The strangest part of the story is that she did not know she had made it: the vocal had been cut earlier for a direct-to-video documentary, and Staton has said she could not remember recording a song by that title at all. Wikipedia quotes her on being told she had a hit in England and asking which song it was.

authors.name: Florence + the Machine
authors.heading: Florence + the Machine
authors.metaLine: British band formed in London, 2007 · Island Records · single released 2009
authors.bio: Florence Welch and Isabella Summers formed the band in London in 2007, and their version — titled “You’ve Got the Love” and produced by Charlie Hugall — became one of the defining British singles of its decade. It first appeared as a B-side to “Dog Days Are Over” in December 2008, went out as a UK digital single in January 2009, was reissued physically in November 2009, and reached No. 5 on the UK Singles Chart across 30 weeks. The record is genuinely wonderful and the band have never hidden that it is a cover; the error is entirely in the listening public’s chronology, not in anything Florence + the Machine claimed.

authors.name: Anthony B. Stephens, Arnecia Michelle Harris and John Bellamy
authors.heading: Stephens, Harris & Bellamy
authors.metaLine: Songwriters credited on “You Got the Love” · also recorded under the name The Source
authors.bio: The composition is credited to Anthony B. Stephens, Arnecia Michelle Harris and John Bellamy. They are not a separate party from the original billing: The Source was their working alias, which is why the 1986 label copy reads “The Source featuring Candi Staton.” Because the video producers who commissioned Staton’s vocal had no money to pay her, they gave her half the copyright and publishing instead — a decision that, once the song became a perennial UK hit, turned out far better for her than a session fee. The name later passed to a different owner: producer John Truelove adopted “The Source” as his own moniker in 1991 for the remixes that finally charted.

misattribution.heading: Setting the record straight
misattribution.intro: The confusion here is chronological, not factual — nobody involved has ever claimed otherwise. It persists because the 1986 record was a commercial non-event and the 2009 cover was inescapable.

items.who: Florence + the Machine wrote and originated it
items.why: Their version, titled “You’ve Got the Love,” was released on Island in 2008–2009 and reached No. 5 in the UK. It is a cover, and the band have always presented it as one.

items.who: The Source featuring Candi Staton, Streetwave, 1986
items.why: A UK 12″ single, catalogue MKHAN 78, licensed by DJ Simon Harris and released by Morgan Khan. It did not chart on release.

items.who: Anthony B. Stephens, Arnecia Michelle Harris and John Bellamy

items.who: Sky Sports, Sex and the City, Gossip Girl and Layer Cake used the Source version, not Florence’s

misattribution.truthLine: First released 1986, by The Source featuring Candi Staton, on Streetwave — and it was a hit twice over before Florence Welch ever sang it.

context.heading: How a record nobody bought became a song everybody knows
lead: The usual story of an eclipsed original is that the cover simply outsold it. This one is stranger, because the 1986 record was never really in the race. It was a 12″ on Streetwave that did not chart at all, built around a vocal Candi Staton had taped for a direct-to-video documentary about a man trying to lose weight, and which she had forgotten making. There was no hit to eclipse — only a piece of vinyl circulating among DJs.

What made the song famous was not the original release and not, at first, Florence Welch. It was a bootleg: London DJ Eren Abdullah laid Staton’s a cappella over the instrumental of Frankie Knuckles and Jamie Principle’s house record “Your Love,” and that hybrid, released commercially in 1991, reached No. 4 in Britain. Remixes in 1997 and 2006 went to No. 3 and No. 7. So by the time Florence + the Machine recorded it, the song had already been a UK top-five hit three separate times — which is precisely the history the 2009 audience never encountered.
context.detailsSummary: The full chronology, and which version soundtracked what
detailsBody: Earlier in the 1980s: Candi Staton records the vocal for a direct-to-video documentary. The producers cannot pay her and assign her half the copyright and publishing instead.
1986: DJ Simon Harris finds and licenses the track; Morgan Khan releases it on Streetwave as a 12″ single credited to The Source featuring Candi Staton. It does not chart.

1989–1991: DJ Eren Abdullah’s mash of Staton’s vocal with “Your Love” circulates as a bootleg; John Truelove issues it commercially in 1991 under the name The Source. It enters the UK chart on 2 February 1991 and peaks at No. 4.
1997: React Music’s “Now Voyager Mix” reaches No. 3, the song’s highest UK position.
2006: The “New Voyager Mix” on Positiva reaches No. 7.

2008–2009: Florence + the Machine’s “You’ve Got the Love” appears as a B-side in December 2008, then as a UK digital single in January 2009 on Island, with a physical reissue in November 2009. It peaks at No. 5.

A correction worth making: the syncs most often credited to Florence largely are not hers. Wikipedia places the Sex and the City and Gossip Girl finales, the Layer Cake club scene and Sky Sports’ Football League theme (used until the 2014–15 season) with versions of the Source recording. The Florence sync that measurably moved the needle was the Gavin & Stacey finale on 1 January 2010, after which her single climbed 18 places to No. 13.
context.pull: A record that did not chart, sung by a woman who had forgotten singing it.

rights.note: The composition is credited to Anthony B. Stephens, Arnecia Michelle Harris and John Bellamy, with half the copyright and publishing assigned to Candi Staton, and remains controlled by those writers and their publishers.
